home.seoDescription: Jungology is a free Jung Functions Quiz: an educational reading of Jung’s eight function-attitudes — thinking, feeling, sensation, and intuition, each extraverted or introverted. No account.
home.title: Jungology
home.lede: The statements follow Psychological Types, taking each function as it turns toward the outer world or toward the inner impression a thing leaves, and what you get is a sketch of how the psyche orients rather than a verdict on who you are, which is a reading, and therefore incomplete, as all such readings are.

steps.title: Answer forty-eight statements
steps.body: Each one is a single claim about how you notice, decide, or take in a situation. Tap how true it is. The whole set takes most people about eight minutes.

steps.title: A short follow-up, only if needed
steps.body: If two answers finish too close for a type, you get a few forced choices at the end — not another full quiz — and then the reading.

steps.title: Read it as a map
steps.body: The closest type is then shown as eight archetypal roles, from the leading function to its most unconscious counterpart, which is a map of the psyche, not a fixed definition of the person.

home.functionsIntro: Jung argued that we all use every function, though we prefer some and struggle with others, and extraversion and introversion here mean where the function points — toward the outer world, or toward the inner impression a thing leaves — not whether you are sociable.

faq.a: In Psychological Types (1921), Jung described four functions — thinking, feeling, sensation, and intuition — each of which can turn toward the outer world or toward the inner impression a thing leaves, and that gives eight function-attitudes. This quiz then reads your scores through Beebe’s later eight-role model.

faq.q: Is this the official MBTI® test?
faq.a: No. This is a free educational quiz inspired by Jung’s functions. The Myers-Briggs Type Indicator is a separate, trademarked instrument, and we report your eight function scores first, then a likely four-letter type as a reading aid.

faq.q: How long does the quiz take?
faq.a: There are forty-eight statements. Tap a number to move on. Most people finish in about eight minutes. If two answers are too close, a few extra choices come after the forty-eight, not in the middle.
There is no account. Your answers stay in this browser until you start over, and they are not sent to a server. Cloudflare and Google Analytics may count page views, not answers.

faq.q: What if two attitudes are equally strong, as Fi and Ti both at 88%?
faq.a: When two functions land that close, the forty-eight items are not enough, so after the quiz you get a short follow-up: which sentence sounds more like you. Those answers are folded into the percentages. If they still split, you can try a different lead on the results page.

faq.q: What is Your Type in Depth?
faq.a: The quiz, the eight scores, and the choice of leading and supporting functions stay free, while Your Type in Depth is a longer reading of why two functions were close, the weaker end of the type, Beebe’s eight roles, and notes on growth, which you can print.

A separate purchase from Your Type in Depth, it reads the other fifteen types against your own functions, not as a ranking of who you should date, but as a picture of where someone else’s leading function already sits in you.

about.seoDescription: How this quiz uses Psychological Types and Beebe’s eight-role model to score the eight function-attitudes.
about.title: About
about.lede: This quiz scores the eight function-attitudes as Jung set them down in Psychological Types (1921), and then reads that profile through Beebe’s later eight-role model, which is a map of the psyche rather than a verdict on who you are.

sections.heading: What Jung measured
paragraphs: Jung distinguished four functions — thinking, feeling, sensation, and intuition — each able to turn toward the object (extraverted) or toward the subjective factor (introverted). That gives eight function-attitudes. Extraversion here is not sociability; it is whether the function is oriented by the outer object or by the inner impression of the object.

sections.heading: The item bank
paragraphs: There are forty-eight original statements, six for each function-attitude. You rate each from 1 to 5, and a tap moves you on. If two functions are still close after the forty-eight, a short follow-up at the end names the lead. The totals appear as 0–100% bars.

sections.heading: Beebe’s eight roles
paragraphs: Beebe argued that a type is not four functions but eight, each carrying an archetypal charge: Hero, Good Parent, Puer/Puella (Child), Anima/Animus, Opposing Personality, Senex/Witch, Trickster, and Demon/Daimon. The shadow four are the same functions as the ego four, with the opposite attitude. The quiz first scores all eight attitudes, then finds the classical stack whose Beebe pattern best fits that profile, with the leading function weighted first.

sections.heading: How a type is suggested
paragraphs: Each of the sixteen types is scored with the leading function first, so a type whose dominant function is not your strongest score is set aside, while the supporting function is rewarded next, the third moderately, and the inferior only slightly. The model also wants the lead to outrank its opposite-attitude twin. If two functions score close, free results let you pick the lead and the support, and Your Type in Depth opens Child, Anima, and the full eight-role stack.

When two functions land together — Fi and Ti both high, or Ni and Ne — the totals are not enough, so after the forty-eight the quiz asks a short follow-up: five forced choices between those two, not another set of ratings. Those answers are folded into the percentages, the winner’s bar rises and the other falls, and that is what names the lead. If they still split, you can try a different lead on the results page.

sections.heading: Your Type in Depth
paragraphs: The quiz, the eight scores, and a Hero / Parent pick stay free, while the close-score reading, Child and Anima, the full eight-role stack, and the longer chapters sit behind a one-time unlock. Set a Lemon Squeezy or Stripe Payment Link as VITE_DOSSIER_CHECKOUT_URL and put the fulfillment keys in VITE_DOSSIER_UNLOCK_KEYS. After payment, send people to /type-in-depth?key=their-key.

sections.heading: Compatibility add-on
paragraphs: Compatibility is a second, separate unlock. It places the other fifteen types on your Beebe stack (same stack, hero and parent swapped, anima pull, and so on). Use VITE_COMPAT_CHECKOUT_URL and VITE_COMPAT_UNLOCK_KEYS, and send people to /compatibility?key=their-key. A Type in Depth key will not open compatibility, and a compatibility key will not open Your Type in Depth.

sections.heading: What this is not
paragraphs: This is not psychotherapy, not a medical assessment, and not the Myers-Briggs Type Indicator. MBTI® is a registered trademark of the Myers-Briggs Type Indicator Trust. Jung wrote about functions as living processes. Beebe’s roles describe how those processes can appear in the psyche, not a box you cannot leave.

sections.heading: Privacy
paragraphs: There is no account and no database of answers. Optional Cloudflare Web Analytics may count page visits such as /quiz and /results; the answers themselves stay in this browser and are never sent to a server.

mapPage.auxiliaryLead: Do not try to develop the inferior function. That would be like telling a fish to learn how to live on land. The work, for every type, is the auxiliary — Beebe’s good parent, the sublimation function — whose basic purpose is to heal the schism between the dominant and the inferior.
mapPage.antiTypeLead: Under stress you can start expressing your anti-type — the type whose dominant and auxiliary are the inverted attitudes of yours. Introversion or extraversion stays, and so does sensing or intuition; thinking/feeling and judging/perceiving flip. What shows is a crude, temporary version of that other type. It is stress. It is not a new type.
